clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to exercise, without further presidential action, the authority conferred on the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 U.S.C. 211a) to prescribe passport rules. The section has no duration or condition, no held instrument amends or revokes it, and the 2025 and 2026 held documents treat the delegation as current.

Terminated on 1966-08-05 by performance. This is the section 2 lead-in ("Subject to Section 3 of this order, the following are hereby superseded"). The words "are hereby superseded" make it a one-time command that operates on issuance, with no later act required, and the order states no effective date later than signing. The order was signed on August 5, 1966 and filed for publication on August 8, 1966; the signing date is recorded, and the exclusive alternative is the filing date. The superseded orders' rules survive only through section 3, which is a separate continuing clause, and no later instrument is claimed as the end.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 211a (release point 119-121) prints section 3 as part of the order in force and states no ending; no held instrument revokes the order or the saving, and the saved rules continue by the clause's own words until revoked or amended under the order's authority unless sooner terminated by operation of law.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14 as a standing saving clause. Section 3 provides that the rules and regulations contained in the superseded orders, and those issued under their authority, that were in force when the order was issued remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended in pursuance of the authority conferred by this order, "unless sooner terminated by operation of law". The clause has no date or event that ends it; no held instrument revokes or amends it; and the passport rule-making it preserves continues under section 1. No held source identifies an individual saved rule that is still in force or that ended, which is disclosed rather than inferred.

research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 11295 of August 5, 1966, Rules Governing the Granting, Issuing, and Verifying of United States Passports (31 FR 10603; FR Doc. 66-8711, filed August 8, 1966), read in full from the official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11295.txt. Under 3 U.S.C. 301 it has three sections: section 1 designates and empowers the Secretary of State to exercise, without further presidential action, the authority conferred on the President by the first section of the Act of July 3, 1926 (22 U.S.C. 211a) to designate and prescribe rules governing the granting, issuing and verifying of passports; section 2 supersedes Executive Order 7856 (March 31, 1938) and Executive Order 8820 (July 11, 1941), subject to section 3; section 3 saves the rules and regulations in those orders, and those issued under their authority, that were in force when this order was issued. The recital is not an operative clause. The five machine clauses (section 1, the section 2 lead-in, section 2(1), section 2(2) and section 3) cover the whole operative text and are confirmed without correction. Ending search: the order states no duration, condition or sunset. The held corpus was searched for the number 11295. The later orders and notices that name it do not amend, revoke or supersede it: Executive Order 14348 (September 5, 2025; 90 FR 43895, section 3(d)) names it as an authority for geographic passport restrictions, and Federal Register notices 2017-25441, 2018-03801 and 2026-17655 recite it as the delegation to the Secretary of State. The Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for this order list only its own provisional supersession of Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 and a see-reference to Executive Order 14348 and 55 FR 3676, none of which ends it. Current predicate: the U.S. Code note under 22 U.S.C. 211a (release point 119-121) prints the order as provided; 22 U.S.C. 211a and 3 U.S.C. 301 remain in the Code; 22 CFR parts 22 and 51 (repository-held CFR text, not cited as evidence) cite the order in their authority lines. Bounded searches read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences in saved order texts). Date note: the order contains no separate effective-date clause, so the one-time supersession in section 2 is recorded as performed on the signing date, August 5, 1966; the alternative reading is that it took effect when the order was filed for publication (August 8, 1966).

savings.reason: Section 3 saves the rules and regulations contained in Executive Orders 7856 and 8820 and those issued under their authority that were in force on issuance, to remain in effect until revoked or amended in pursuance of the authority this order confers, unless sooner terminated by operation of law. No held instrument revokes the order or terminates that saving; no held source identifies a particular saved rule that survives or ended, which is disclosed. The passport rule-making authority continues under section 1.
